    Pong

    The main class for the Pong game. It extends the Game class and implements the game logic, including player controls, ball movement, collision detection, and score tracking.

      • calculateScaleFactor

        private double calculateScaleFactor()
        Calculate the scale factor based on the current window size and the base resolution. The scale factor is used to scale the size and speed of game objects to maintain consistent gameplay across different window sizes. The scale factor is the minimum of the width scale and height scale, ensuring that the game objects fit within the window without distortion.
        Returns:
        the scale factor as a floating number

        public void reset()
        Reset the ball to the center of the screen, and reset the paddles to the edges of the screen Paused the game for 3 seconds for the players to be ready. Uses proportions of the screen size to set the positions of the ball and paddles, so it works for any screen size.

      • resetBallPhantoms

        private void resetBallPhantoms()
        Reset the ball phantoms by removing them from the game and clearing the list. This is called when a player scores to ensure that any existing phantom balls are removed from the game before the next round starts

      • powerUpCollision

        private void powerUpCollision()
        Check the collision of the ball with the phantom power up. If the ball collides with the power up, a phantom ball is spawned, and the power up disappears. The phantom ball will have the same size as the main ball, but will move slower and will disappear after hitting a paddle once. The power up will reappear after a random interval.

      • phantomCollision

        private void phantomCollision()
        Check the collision of phantoms

      • ballBounce

        private void ballBounce()
        Check the collision of ball object with other game objects such as the paddle that make the ball bounce back. If the ball collides with the top or bottom bounds, it will bounce back. If the ball collides with a paddle, it will bounce back and adjust its vertical velocity based on the paddle's vertical velocity. The ball will also play a bounce sound effect when it collides with a paddle or the top/bottom bounds.
